title: Masquerade at Ashford House
victim: Cordelia Ashford, hostess of the ball
teaser: At midnight the guests took off their masks, but the hostess never took off hers. Cordelia Ashford was found in the winter garden with a white porcelain mask on her face and a black tear painted under one eye. Three such masks were seen during the evening, the guests swapped costumes all through the ball, and nobody can swear who they danced the last waltz with.
professions: Driver of the new motor car

habits.label: Raven feathers
habits.habit: A cloak sewn with black raven feathers
clues: A black raven feather with a bit of thread on its quill is stuck to the wet tiles by the fountain in the winter garden. The culprit has a cloak with raven feathers.
Three raven feathers are caught on the brass stair rod of the runner on the servants' stairs. The culprit has a cloak sewn with raven feathers.

habits.label: Powder on the collar
habits.habit: Collar dusted with white rice powder
clues: The dark leather of a library armchair has a white smear of rice powder exactly where the back touches the neck. The culprit's collar is dusted with rice powder.
In the winter garden the hostess's black velvet shoulder has white rice powder on it, and Cordelia never powdered. The culprit has powder on their collar.

habits.label: Lace fan
habits.habit: Never lets go of a black lace fan
clues: In the portrait gallery, under the portrait of the late Mr Ashford, lies a broken tortoiseshell blade with a scrap of black lace. The culprit has a black lace fan.
Nobody takes fans into the smoking room, yet a black lace tassel from a fan was dropped on the baize of the card table. The culprit has a black lace fan.

habits.label: Dance card
habits.habit: A dance card with a silver pencil
clues: A leaf from a dance card was found in the lemon tree tub in the winter garden, and the last waltz on it is written illegibly. The culprit has a dance card.
Under a chair by the ballroom wall lies a little silver pencil on a silk cord, the kind used to fill in dance cards. The culprit has a dance card with a silver pencil.

habits.label: Plague doctor mask
habits.habit: A plague doctor mask with a long beak
clues: In the costume wardrobe the plague doctor mask hangs on the wrong hook, and dry cloves, still fragrant, are falling out of the beak. The culprit wears a plague doctor mask.
In the winter garden the misted glass has the mark of a long beak, as if someone pressed their masked face to it. The culprit wears a plague doctor mask.

habits.label: Bells on the costume
habits.habit: Columbine's bells jingle on their costume
clues: The scullery maid on the servants' stairs heard a quick jingle of bells above her, then a door slammed. The culprit has bells on their costume.
A brass bell with its loop torn off lies on the carpet in the portrait gallery. The culprit has bells on their costume.

habits.label: Violet pastilles
clues: There's a lilac sweet wrapper on the library windowsill, and a sweet smell of violets around it. The culprit sucks violet pastilles.
An empty tin of violet pastilles was dropped behind the curtain in the ballroom. The culprit sucks violet pastilles.

habits.label: Monocle on a cord
habits.habit: A monocle on a black silk cord
clues: A monocle lies on the library carpet, a scrap of black silk cord still tied to its eye. The culprit has a monocle on a cord.
A waiter carrying ice to the smoking room noticed a round lens flash in someone's eye in the half-dark. The culprit wears a monocle.

habits.label: Smells of cigars
clues: Smoking is forbidden in the winter garden because of the orchids, yet it smells strongly of Havana cigar. The culprit smells of cigars.
In the costume wardrobe Death's velvet cloak reeks of cigar smoke, though it was never worn into the smoking room. The culprit smells of Havana cigars.

habits.label: Velvet beauty spot
habits.habit: A velvet beauty spot above the lip
clues: A tiny circle of black velvet with a drop of glue lies on the smoking room carpet. The culprit wears a velvet beauty spot above the lip.
A glass left on the library windowsill has a trace of glue and a black velvet crumb right at the rim. The culprit wears a velvet beauty spot above the lip.

habits.label: Sapphire ring
habits.habit: A ring with a large sapphire
clues: A faceted blue stone, a sapphire, that fell out of its setting lies under a window in the portrait gallery. The culprit has a sapphire ring.
A waiter in the smoking room noticed a ring with a blue stone the size of a pea on the hand holding a glass. The culprit has a ring with a large sapphire.

habits.label: Stammers when nervous
clues: The cook on the servants' stairs heard a voice upstairs stumble three times on the first syllable: "C-c-cordelia." The culprit stammers.
A guest dozing in the library heard an argument from behind the shelves, and one voice stumbled over every word. The culprit stammers when nervous.

habits.label: Silver-headed cane
habits.habit: A cane with a silver dog's head
clues: A silver ear broken off a handle shaped like a dog's head was found under a chair by the ballroom wall. The culprit has a cane with a silver dog's head.
On the sand of the winter garden path, next to the shoe prints, there are round holes from a cane every other step. The culprit has a silver-headed cane.

habits.label: Inky finger
habits.habit: Middle finger stained with violet ink
clues: In the library the page of an open book has a violet print of a middle finger. The culprit has a finger stained with violet ink.
In the portrait gallery the gilded frame of the hostess's portrait has a little spot of violet ink. The culprit's middle finger is stained with violet ink.

habits.label: Creaky shoes
habits.habit: New shoes that creak at every step
clues: A maid ironing dresses in the costume wardrobe heard new shoes creaking down the corridor step after step. The culprit has creaky shoes.
The guests in the smoking room fell silent when someone walked past the door in creaking new shoes, and everyone remembered that creak. The culprit has creaky new shoes.

habits.label: Chrysanthemum buttonhole
habits.habit: A white chrysanthemum in the buttonhole
clues: In the portrait gallery, under the portrait of old Mr Ashford, lies a broken white chrysanthemum stem. The culprit has a chrysanthemum in their buttonhole.
In the costume wardrobe a white chrysanthemum petal is stuck to a monk's habit right by the collar. The culprit wears a white chrysanthemum in their buttonhole.

keys: The winter garden is locked after eleven so the guests don't crush the orchids, yet the door was opened with a key and locked again. The culprit had keys.
The costume wardrobe was locked before midnight, yet the third porcelain mask was taken out of it without force. The culprit had keys.
sched: It all happened during the interval the orchestra in the ballroom takes at a quarter past twelve according to the programme. The culprit knows the schedule.
The winter garden is checked at midnight and at half past twelve, and someone was there exactly between the rounds. The culprit knows the schedule.
passages: A door behind a bookcase leads from the library to the winter garden. Only the servants know about it, and the dust on its threshold has been rubbed away. The culprit knows the service passages.
The servants' stairs lead to the orangery through a storeroom of flowerpots, and the storeroom floor has fresh prints of ballroom shoes. The culprit knows the service passages.
quiet: The gravel on the winter garden paths crunches under any heel, yet Cordelia didn't even turn round. The culprit moves silently.
The old parquet in the portrait gallery answers every step, yet a guest dozing there on a banquette heard no one. The culprit moves silently.
safe: The fireproof safe in the library where the new will lay was opened with the combination, and the envelope is empty. The culprit knows the safe combination.
The pearls for announcing the engagement were taken from the safe behind a portrait in the portrait gallery, and the lock hasn't a scratch. The culprit knows the safe combination.
french: A card reading "Les masques tombent à minuit", French for "The masks fall at midnight", is pinned to the porcelain mask in the winter garden. The culprit knows French.
In the library a volume of Baudelaire in French lies open, and a line about a mask is underlined in fresh pencil. The culprit knows French.
cash: The envelope with the orchestra's wages in the smoking room was opened and sealed again, and a third of the money is missing. The culprit had access to money.
In the estate ledger lying in the library, three sums for the month have been scraped out and the figures written in an imitation of the hostess's hand. The culprit had access to money.
driver: The cook saw from the servants' stair window during the waltz how a car's headlights moved from the garage to the orangery and back. The culprit can drive.
In the costume wardrobe, under Death's cloak, lie driving goggles and gauntlets, and the gauntlets have fresh road mud on them. The culprit can drive.
medic: A champagne glass dropped in the winter garden smells of bitter almonds. The culprit knows about poisons.
A bottle of foxglove tincture is missing from the household medicine chest by the servants' stairs, and its cork turned up in the ballroom. The culprit knows about poisons.
tech: The electric light in the winter garden went out for four minutes: a fuse in the box under the servants' stairs was pulled and put back. The culprit knows their way around machinery.
The bell from the winter garden to the servants' hall was silent all evening: its wire in the smoking room had been neatly disconnected from the battery. The culprit knows their way around machinery.
tools: The spring on the door from the winter garden to the yard was unhooked with pliers so the door wouldn't bang, then hooked back on. The culprit is handy with tools.
The display case in the costume wardrobe where the porcelain masks lay was opened by removing the beading, and the glass sits in place as good as new. The culprit is handy with tools.
strong: The palm tub in the winter garden, which four gardeners move together, was shifted a full pace. The culprit is physically strong.
The smoking room door was barricaded from inside with a heavy leather sofa. The culprit is physically strong.
